correctness.rationale: Each commuting partial injection is uniquely a decorated partial matching between nilpotent alpha chains. The position increment criterion isolates exactly fully aligned equal-length cycles as the obstruction to nilpotence. Inclusion-exclusion over disjoint forbidden cycles is reduced by the signed-permutation identity to the one-chain-per-length deletion sieve. The uniform-case path/cycle exponential formula and coefficientwise rank-shift law follow. Independent direct point-map enumeration for every partition of up to six points, matching-sieve comparisons through size eleven for up to five chains, and exact uniform EGF checks passed. The proof applies to every partition; finite checks are corroboration only.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete rank-by-rank census of nilpotents inside the centralizer of every nilpotent partial injection (indexed by all chain partitions), a natural invariant at the intersection of two basic semigroup properties. The cancellation from cycle inclusion-exclusion to deletion of at most one chain per distinct length is a structural simplification, not a small fixed-size table. The uniform family yields the unexpected exact identity that the rank-r nonnilpotent count equals c times the rank-(r-L) unrestricted count for one fewer chain, furnishing interpretable exact benchmarks.
